Recorded specifications: {"availability": "Public Python source published on PyPI and the AUR; runs need an OpenRouter or Vercel AI Gateway key (or a TypeSafe key) and a Browser Use Cloud key unless local Chrome or a CDP endpoint is used.", "package_version": "0.5.23", "repository_revision": "d35f75f43e4e2ed42edb4edec72843435af73a0b"}

Python package fastbrowse 0.5.23 by Agent Labs (Python 3.13+), with a CLI, an MCP server (fastbrowse-mcp) and a JavaScript SDK. The browser layer speaks CDP through cdp-use; snapshot.js, ported from jev-ultrafast, indexes each frame's controls, viewport text and a freshness fingerprint, including open shadow roots. Per the design document, Jev chooses the operation and target among indexed controls (with relevance pruning on dense pages), an LLM proposes start addresses, plans checkable requirements, reads page text, writes non-secret field text and composes the answer, and code enforces freshness and hit-tests before input, no automatic retry of mutations, authorization for submit, pay, delete or send, secret redaction and budgets; a run counts as complete only when every requirement is evidenced. Browsers are Browser Use Cloud by default, local Chrome, or an existing CDP endpoint including Electron windows. Jev is reached through TypeSafe, OpenRouter or the Vercel AI Gateway. Benchmark comparisons in the README are the publisher's. Root LICENSE is MIT, with a NOTICE file.

This covers the released weights only; the README warns that parts of the training data are research-only or subject to a model provider's terms."}}, "training_data_note": "Publisher-listed sources: Mind2Web and NNetNav-live browser steps (NNetNav stop labels relabelled by an LLM judge), judge-verified teacher episodes from jev-ultrafast runs on live sites with qwen3-max and later GLM-5.3-Flash as System One, and general typed-decision corpora (Kev decision-v7, typed-decisions, tasksource-jev, jev-distill, typed-decisions-synth). The README warns that some tasksource-jev tasks are research-only and that teacher episodes are model outputs under their provider's terms."}

Models and code for an open replacement of a hosted System One decision API. A Qwen3 or Qwen3.5 backbone without its vocabulary head scores each option with a pointer head, so one pass answers every question in a request; a local server exposes POST /v1/systemone. Browser steps arrive as page text, numbered elements and recent actions, and the model chooses an operation (click, type, DONE and others) and a target element. The repository holds the wev package (data conversion for Mind2Web, NNetNav and WebChain, training, calibration, export, serving), teacher-collection scripts, the OpenJev-Bench browser-lane client (2,346 frozen steps stored in the Hub dataset alanhuangya/OpenJev-Data), locked results and the paper source; the paper is a Zenodo deposit (doi 10.5281/zenodo.22941164) with no catalog record. The models also answer general decisions such as triage and routing. Results are publisher-reported, and live-website numbers use an LLM judge.

Browser application by VilelaLab with Windows and macOS builds (release v1.9.2). The agent loop observes each page through an injected script or the CDP accessibility tree (src/renderer/page-executor.ts), adds tesseract.js OCR text, and attaches a page screenshot only when the configured model accepts images (src/main/ai-engine.ts); clicks and keys go through Electron sendInputEvent on the page (src/main/main.ts). Tools include element-reference clicks and fills, coordinate clicks, tabs and navigation, plus non-interface skills such as image generation, video and price lookups. The README states a 25-step cap, confirmation before paying, buying, deleting or entering card data, and a hand-off on CAPTCHAs and login walls. It runs in the user's persistent logged-in session, presents a Chrome user agent and masks navigator.webdriver, and the app also bundles an ad blocker, password manager, media downloader and torrent client. Chrome Manifest V3 extension (manifest version 1.9.1) whose agent loop is built on the pi-agent-core and pi-ai packages. Its tools (src/agent/tools.ts) read a paginated inventory of interactive DOM controls including open shadow roots, inspect forms, click elements or screenshot-pixel coordinates (used for canvas editors such as Google Docs), type, scroll, switch and open tabs, upload files, post to social sites and send webmail; capture_tab_screenshot returns the visible-tab image to the model. Actions run as scripts injected with chrome.scripting that dispatch synthetic pointer and mouse events (src/agent/browser-bridge.ts); the manifest requests no debugger permission. Before showing its human CAPTCHA gate, the bridge makes up to two automatic rounds in which a vision model is asked to click inside detected challenge regions (src/agent/captcha-auto.ts). It acts in the user's logged-in sessions and keeps a memory store with optional parallel worker windows. The README ends with 'MIT', but the inspected tree has no license file.

mcp-remote-macos-use
Resource type: tool
Review status: curated
Scope: core

MCP server that lets an LLM client such as Claude Desktop control a remote Mac through its built-in Screen Sharing, returning screenshots and sending scaled mouse, keyboard, scroll and drag actions over VNC.
Recorded aliases: Remote MacOs Use
Platforms: desktop, macos
Topics: automation, tool-integration

Recorded specifications: {"availability": "Public Python source and Dockerfile; Docker Hub image; no model.", "repository_revision": "58c13c785ce76ad1d37975e9b7aa32303b8d7c22"}

Python MCP server published by baryhuang and distributed as the Docker image buryhuang/mcp-remote-macos-use; the target Mac needs only Screen Sharing enabled, with host, username and password passed as environment variables. Its own RFB client (src/vnc_client.py) supports only Apple Authentication (protocol 30). server.py registers eight tools: remote_macos_get_screen (a PNG screenshot), send_keys, mouse_move, mouse_click, mouse_double_click, mouse_scroll, mouse_drag_n_drop and open_application; action handlers scale the client's coordinates to the remote screen size, and open_application types the app name into Spotlight (Command+Space, text, Return). An optional LiveKit handler adds WebRTC screen sharing when LiveKit variables are set. The server has no model of its own; the MCP client's model decides the actions. Root LICENSE is MIT (copyright peakmojo); the default branch was last committed on 30 April 2025.

OpenBrowser
Resource type: framework
Review status: curated
Scope: core

Python browser-automation framework whose CodeAgent shows a model indexed DOM state and an optional screenshot, then runs the Python it writes against Chrome DevTools Protocol helpers in a persistent namespace.
Recorded aliases: openbrowser-ai
Platforms: web
Topics: web-navigation, automation, tool-integration

Recorded specifications: {"availability": "Public source and PyPI package; hosted cloud version is waitlisted", "repository_revision": "48ec5d9dccad00001a5c7d644b863bf1277bb1e0"}

Published on PyPI as openbrowser-ai. The CodeAgent (src/openbrowser/code_use/service.py) sends a compact serialized DOM state with element indices and, unless vision is turned off, a JPEG screenshot; the model replies with Python that the executor runs in a persistent namespace. The MCP server exposes a single execute_code tool over the same namespace, and a CLI daemon keeps a browser session alive between commands. The repository also holds a hosted-platform backend and frontend, and infra/training with SFT, online GRPO and diffusion-language-model RL code for FormFactory form filling; the README links the two related papers on ResearchGate. Token and latency comparisons with other browser tools are publisher-reported.

Primary source: https://github.com/billy-enrizky/openbrowser-ai

Browserable
Resource type: framework
Review status: curated
Scope: core

Self-hosted browser-agent platform with a JS SDK and REST API: a planner sets high-level steps, and a runner reads a screenshot and a numbered DOM chunk to pick Playwright actions in a local or hosted browser.
Platforms: web
Topics: web-navigation, automation, planning

Recorded specifications: {"availability": "Public source for the self-hosted services, browser service and JS SDK; no hosted service was tested.", "license_components_note": "ui/LICENSE carries a separate MIT notice, copyright 2015 Gil Barbara; the root browserable notice is distinct.", "repository_revision": "a3af19a66560d8bc3ff2c4ed4f9570eb6a66649c"}

Inspected at commit a3af19a6 (27 August 2025). The README sets up a Docker Compose stack (UI server, tasks server, MongoDB, Redis and MinIO) in which the user supplies one LLM key (Gemini, OpenAI or Claude) and a Steel or Hyperbrowser key; tasks/services/browser.js also accepts Browserbase or the repository's own browser service, which launches Playwright Chromium. In tasks/agents/browserable.js the act-on-tab action calls simpleActionHelper, whose loop takes a plain page screenshot and the current chunk of DOM elements with XPaths, asks a planner for high-level steps (replanning after five steps), and asks a runner for a Playwright method, arguments and element number; the older DOM-only and vision act helpers are commented out at that call site. The repository also contains deep-research and generative agents. The README's 90.4% WebVoyager figure is publisher-reported. The README names Stagehand among the open-source projects it builds on. No code was run.

Community Manifest V3 extension that its README describes as a port of browser-use/jev-ultrafast and as unaffiliated with TypeSafe or Browser Use. The content script (src/content/snapshot.ts) lists visible, hit-tested interactive elements with role, accessible name, value and link target, plus up to 6,000 characters of page text; no screenshots are sent. Jev is a hosted model reached through OpenRouter, TypeSafe or Cloudflare Workers AI; TYPE_TEXT values come from an OpenAI-compatible text model. Clicks and keystrokes are dispatched through chrome.debugger (src/background/input.ts), with synthetic DOM events when that is switched off. The README reports 13 of 17 publisher-chosen tasks passing in one recorded headless-Chromium run (docs/e2e-suite-2026-09-19.md), an internal test suite.

Recorded specifications: {"availability": "Public agent scaffold, CLI and Streamlit app; the proxy-lite-3b weights are published separately on Hugging Face.", "license_review": {"code": {"evidence_urls": ["https://raw.githubusercontent.com/convergence-ai/proxy-lite/a4389c599d5f5f77dc18510c879e2e783434766b/LICENSE"], "reason": "The repository LICENSE file states that the work is licensed under CC BY-NC 4.0 (a notice, not the legal code); recorded for code only; it is not applied to the proxy-lite-3b weights or the hosted Proxy service."}}, "package_version": "0.1.0", "repository_revision": "a4389c599d5f5f77dc18510c879e2e783434766b"}

The repository is the scaffold for Convergence AI's proxy-lite-3b model: a CLI (proxy), a Streamlit app and a Runner that loops a solver and a webbrowser environment. By default it calls a demo endpoint on Hugging Face Spaces, which the README reserves for demonstrations; it recommends serving convergence-ai/proxy-lite-3b with vLLM and the hermes tool-call parser for production. The webbrowser environment (src/proxy_lite/environments/webbrowser.py) launches Chromium through Playwright with playwright_stealth, injects JavaScript to find interactable elements, and by default sends a screenshot annotated with numbered bounding boxes plus a text list of the marked elements; earlier screenshots are dropped from the context. BrowserTool exposes goto, google_search, click, type, scroll, back, wait, reload and do_nothing actions addressed by mark_id. The README says the model is meant to complete tasks autonomously and may struggle with logins or user-confirmed steps. Model weights are not in this repository. Code was read.

BrowseGPT
Resource type: agent

Scope: core

Chrome extension with a local Node.js server that lists the visible page's links, buttons and inputs as a numbered outline and asks OpenAI gpt-3.5-turbo for the next CLICK, ENTER_TEXT or NAVIGATE step toward a goal.

Recorded specifications: {"availability": "Public extension and server source with no license file; the published Chrome Web Store build remains uninspected.", "repository_revision": "c86c148ec7862f971fe827e1270684b9c8c41016"}

Inspected at commit c86c148e (23 July 2024), the latest commit on the default branch. The content script assigns IDs to visible, in-viewport elements and sends the first 100 outline lines with the goal, URL and up to five previous steps to the server, whose few-shot prompt asks gpt-3.5-turbo for one JSON command with a reason; the extension then calls click(), enters text or changes the location. Each submission runs one step, and elements already acted on are left out of later outlines. The Manifest V3 extension is labelled version 2.0. The browsegpt.ai site and its llms.txt describe Claude Haiku 4.5 as the default model with OpenAI GPT as an option; the public repository's server calls only the OpenAI API. The Chrome Web Store build remains uninspected. The repository has no license file, so the code license is unknown. No code was run.

With the Jev switch on, a high-confidence Jev decision can execute a click or type without sending the image to the LLM. Models are user-supplied OpenAI-compatible endpoints. Orca

Recorded specifications: {"availability": "Public Rust source, npm package and native release binaries; no model weights; models come from the DeepSeek API.", "repository_revision": "a016619a31739c938627b611ea7b1bc54572e658", "repository_tree_sha": "f59ed9c2c91a4f9aca227d8beb8ecd6146552b0f"}

Published by echoVic as the npm package @blade-ai/orca and native binaries for macOS, Linux and Windows; it is primarily a coding agent that reads and edits code and runs commands with a DeepSeek API key. Computer use is one feature: on macOS 14 or later, in the main interactive TUI session, a `computer` tool backed by the bundled crates/orca-computer-use driver lists and launches apps, observes a window as an accessibility-element outline with ids plus an optional screenshot, and clicks, types, sends keys and scrolls on targets (protocol.rs, observation.rs). Per the computer-use docs, each app needs approval unless a rule or full-auto mode allows it, typing into secure password fields always asks separately, password managers and finance apps are blocked by default, Orca never operates its own host terminal, plan mode only lists and observes, and Esc stops the run. Browser tools used from the separate Pilion Browser come from that host. Root LICENSE is MIT; the latest GitHub release is v0.5.12.

text:
FluidUse
Resource type: framework
Review status: curated
Scope: core

Swift package for local computer use on Apple silicon that reads forms in running Mac apps or browsers through the Accessibility API and fills them with on-device Core ML decision models.
Platforms: desktop, macos, web
Topics: action-prediction, automation, efficiency

Recorded specifications: {"availability": "Public Swift package source, demos and benchmark reports; Core ML model files are downloaded from the Hugging Face Hub on first use.", "repository_revision": "cfba4d3fa4b996d0b680549416caf7aba6be770c", "repository_tree_sha": "9711dfc5ef1255ffc51ee067811018fbaf18ad5b"}

Published by FluidInference; the package targets macOS 14 or later. AccessibilityFormDriver snapshots the focused window of another running app through the macOS Accessibility API into form elements addressed by tokens, writes values through AXValue and presses buttons and checkboxes with AXPress; for Safari, Chrome, Edge, Brave, Arc, Firefox and similar browsers it sends real key events instead, because those apply AXValue writes to the focused field. WebFormDriver does the same for an embedded WKWebView through an injected script. FormSchema renders each field's context and a fixed option list (fill Label: value for each document entity, check, click, skip) for a model to score, and decodes the chosen option into an action. The README's form model is CUA-S1-FORMS, a 706K-parameter form specialist from Cua converted to Core ML; its manager (CuaS1FormsManager) comes from the FluidAudio package dependency. Most of the package consists of on-device Core ML runtimes for general typed-decision, classification, embedding and OCR models (laya, GLiNER 2.5, Kev, Clef, Intern-Decision, SigLIP2 and others) and demos such as Tetris and 2048 players; their scope lies outside GUI operation. Latency and accuracy figures in the README are publisher measurements. Root LICENSE is Apache-2.0; the latest release, v0.3.0, predates the inspected commit.

Android app whose accessibility service serves a local MCP server of phone tools, letting Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode, run in an on-device proot Linux, read the screen, tap, type and open apps.

Requires a 64-bit Android 11+ phone; the README says it was tested on one OnePlus 12 and uses no adb, PC or root. Tools.java registers the phone tools; read_screen walks the accessibility node tree of the visible windows into a numbered list, and tap acts on those nodes or their clickable ancestors, with a separate screenshot tool. The agents (Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode) are installed into an Alpine Linux that Buddy runs under proot and use the user's own plan or OpenCode's free models; no model is bundled. Actions that send, post, buy, delete or change settings go through confirm cards, and per-app Trust, Hard or Smart rules are enforced by the app; the README names prompt injection from on-screen text as the main risk. benchmark/ reports a small timing comparison of seven model and agent pairs on five phone tasks, two runs each, checked by hand on one phone.

text:
Shadow
Resource type: tool
Review status: curated
Scope: core

macOS app that records screen, audio, input events and accessibility trees on-device, builds searchable episodes, and replays learned procedures through AX-first grounding with a LoRA-tuned ShowUI-2B fallback.
Platforms: desktop, macos
Topics: recording, data-generation, grounding, memory, screen-understanding

Recorded specifications: {"availability": "Public Swift and Rust source built locally; models such as ShowUI-2B, Qwen and Whisper are downloaded separately during setup and are not covered by the repository license.", "repository_revision": "5eef3683b0654e1a1123fe63efa015e257efcdb5"}

Requires Apple Silicon, macOS 14 or later and a source build (Swift 6, Rust, XcodeGen). GroundingOracle.swift resolves targets for the Mimicry replay system in four steps: exact accessibility-tree match, fuzzy accessibility match, a local ShowUI-2B model on MLX over a live screenshot, then a vision-model escalation. TrainingDataGenerator.swift turns recorded (screenshot, accessibility state, click) tuples into JSONL grounding examples, and LoRATrainer.swift fine-tunes ShowUI-2B on them through the mlx-vlm Python package once enough new tuples accumulate. The README describes the capture of fourteen signal types, on-device Qwen and Whisper models, a 26-tool agent runtime, and points to a separate computer-use engine from the same publisher for full computer use. Cloud model features are optional with the user's own API key.

text:
ClosePaw
Resource type: agent
Review status: curated
Scope: core

On-device Android agent app that reads the accessibility tree, with optional screenshots, acts through accessibility node actions or gesture taps, and can run on a Shizuku virtual display in the background.
Platforms: android
Topics: mobile-navigation, human-in-the-loop, memory

Recorded specifications: {"availability": "Source and a signed APK attached to GitHub release v0.1.0", "release_tag": "v0.1.0", "repository_revision": "75dae2653f5a6b25d5df51ee7008b0f830de1536"}

Kotlin app for Android 12 or later with an on-device ReAct loop, subagent delegation, todo and scratchpad tools, markdown memory files and per-app skills. Perception defaults to the accessibility tree; screenshot-only and hybrid modes are options (perception/PerceptionConfig.kt). Clicks try an accessibility ACTION_CLICK on the resolved node and fall back to a dispatched gesture tap (tool/action/ClickExecutor.kt, platform/NodeActionPerformer.kt, platform/AccessibilityGestureInjector.kt). Optional power tools use Shizuku for a background virtual display, Termux for a Linux shell, and Chrome DevTools Protocol scripting of Chrome. A bundled tier list blocks banking, payment, crypto-wallet, password-manager and authenticator packages (assets/security/app_tiers.json), and other apps need per-app approval. Models are reached through OpenAI-compatible endpoints or a ChatGPT/Codex sign-in. The eval/ harness drives AndroidWorld task setup and scoring and launches the app over ADB.

initAgents.ts defines an app-selection agent and an action agent, both configured with gpt-4.1-mini through the OpenAI Agents SDK; the name is unrelated to Anthropic's Claude Opus models, and an OpenAI API key is required. Each action step receives the target app's AppleScript dictionary, a list of clickable Accessibility elements (role, title, value, help and description) and, when captured, a screenshot (runAgents.ts). Swift helpers under app/swift read the Accessibility tree, click, send keys and move the app window to a separate virtual display so the agent can work in the background. The repository also contains the tryop.us landing site and a small server.

No model is bundled.", "package_version": "0.1.4", "release_tag": "v0.1.4", "repository_revision": "7cc6b3d6d25ae6064aa1cf56d32df3af6e24a212"}

Published on npm as @agent-ctrl/cli (package.json and Cargo.toml 0.1.4; annotated tag v0.1.4 points at the inspected commit), with release binaries for Windows x64 and macOS arm64/x64 and a typed @agent-ctrl/client TypeScript wrapper. agent-ctrl open <surface> starts a per-session daemon; snapshot pins a target window and returns its accessibility tree with @eN action refs and @sN scope refs, which click, type, fill, select, check, scroll, drag, press, wait and find commands consume. Screenshots of a window, region, element or the desktop can be annotated with cached refs. Windows (crates/surface-uia, UI Automation patterns plus SendInput) and macOS (crates/surface-ax, Accessibility plus CGEvent input) have the full action vocabulary; Linux (crates/surface-atspi) only snapshots, finds, inspects and lists windows, and Android and iOS surfaces are planned. The README leaves browser automation to the separate agent-browser project. The tool contains no model or agent loop.

Code release of the ICLR 2026 paper "LongHorizonUI: A Unified Framework for Robust long-horizon Task Automation of GUI Agent" (the repository description says ICLR2026; the README cites it with anonymous authors and no link). Each screenshot passes through RapidOCR, the OmniParser v2 YOLO icon detector (downloaded from microsoft/OmniParser-v2.0 on first use) and template matching when an icon template directory is set; the merged elements are drawn as numbered boxes, and that annotated screenshot with a step prompt is what the Gemini, Azure OpenAI or OpenAI model receives. Actions are click, long press, swipe, drag, text input and key press. With the fallback cascade on (the default), an element-index target that fails is retried as a relative point inside the box and then as absolute coordinates with jitter; a progress monitor can roll back to the last committed snapshot, at most three times per task. The README documents only the offline mode, which replays a task's recorded screenshot sequence with either the task description or step-by-step instructions. run.py also has a live subcommand that lists USB-connected devices, but at the reviewed commit AndroidContext never opens a device connection (its context stays None), so device actions return without acting. The repository also has a Gradio app, agents that turn recorded taps and swipes into step descriptions, a scrcpy-based Android recording tool, step-level evaluation scripts and the project page source. The LongGUIBench dataset is not released (the README link is a placeholder), the requirements.txt the README installs from is not in the tree, and the README's Apache-2.0 badge and LICENSE link are not backed by a license file. Not a fork, not archived; no release.

Published on npm as agent-cu (package.json 0.1.1 at the inspected commit) with precompiled binaries, and also installable as an agent skill (skills/agent-computer-use/SKILL.md). Commands snapshot an app's accessibility tree into @eN refs or query it with a selector DSL (role, name, id, parent-child chains), then click, type, press keys, scroll, drag, move or resize windows, wait for elements, take screenshots, and run JSON batches or YAML workflows; output is JSON by default. Backends: macOS uses AXUIElement with CGEvent input, Windows uses UI Automation, and Linux uses AT-SPI2 over D-Bus with xdotool for input. Electron apps can be driven over the Chrome DevTools Protocol, but automatic Electron detection and relaunch with a debug port is implemented only on macOS (cli/crates/agent-computer-use-cdp/src/detect.rs). The README marks every platform as preview and states that the project is no longer maintained, recommending Cua Driver instead. The repository was formerly named kortix-ai/agent-click (same GitHub repository ID). The tool contains no model or agent loop.

Kotlin Android app for Android 11 (API 30) or later, published by KUAFUAI, with a floating-ball persona, voice input and output, an encrypted on-device notebook and scheduled scenes. One AccessibilityService is the entry point. ScreenController.kt renders the pruned accessibility tree as an outline with one line per element, an element id, a clickable mark and a centre in 0-1000 relative coordinates; for apps that draw their own pixels the model gets a screenshot (accessibility takeScreenshot, or MediaProjection per ScreenCapture.kt) overlaid with an 8-column by 12-row labelled grid, taps by cell and which third of it, and can request a zoomed view with a red crosshair before committing. A per-location guard refuses a fourth tap within 120 px of the same spot inside five minutes. Text goes in through the accessibility input channel on Android 13 or later, with ADBKeyboard as the fallback. LocalBrain.kt runs a non-streaming tool-calling loop against any OpenAI-compatible endpoint for a configurable number of steps (1 to 200); the brain can instead run elsewhere and reach the device over a WebSocket hub. The README states that the dispatcher stops before a purchase's final confirmation, never enters payment passwords, and types vault passwords without returning them to the model. Optional extras include a robot dog driven through a USB OTG dongle. The mg CLI pulls a prebuilt Docker runtime with the Android emulator and the MemGUI AVD snapshot, launches parallel backend containers on a Linux host with KVM, runs agents through MobileWorld's agent interface (src/mobile_world) and writes MobileWorld-format trajectories with screenshots. MemGUI-Eval (memgui_eval/) describes each step with a multimodal model and makes a final decision with a second model; the leaderboard uses Gemini 2.5 Flash and Gemini 2.5 Pro for these roles. Each task CSV row gives the app(s), difficulty, whether UI memory is required and golden steps; the default step budget is int(golden_steps * 2.5 + 1). The Hugging Face dataset lgy0404/MemGUI-Bench holds the same two task CSV files (byte-identical at revisions 217713e and 3fb01b6), so it is recorded as an alias.

The README runs tasks with the OSWorld runner (Chrome in an Ubuntu VM, 100-step budget) after converting them with convert_odysseys_to_osworld.py, whose OSWorld evaluator is a placeholder; scoring is done afterwards by run_full_trajectory_per_rubric.py, which asks an LLM judge (by default gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview, the model the README uses, or an OpenAI-compatible model) whether any step satisfies each rubric item. TipTour
Resource type: agent
Review status: curated
Scope: core

macOS menu-bar agent that grounds clicks with a local Core ML control detector and accessibility tree, driven by TypeSafe's JEV text loop or Gemini realtime voice, with a localhost harness for other agents.
Platforms: desktop, macos
Topics: grounding, screen-understanding, human-in-the-loop

Recorded specifications: {"availability": "Public source built with Xcode; no release binaries; JEV, Gemini and Elorian features need the user's own API keys"}

JEV mode sends the typed task, locally detected labels and positions, and action history to TypeSafe's hosted jev-latest model (api.typesafe.ai); it performs only clicks and stops after 12 actions. Gemini mode receives microphone audio and, when enabled, screenshots. Video tours are built by the Elorian service and only point at controls. The localhost harness on 127.0.0.1:19474 exposes observe, ground-target and act endpoints. Requires macOS 14.2+ and an Xcode build; the repository has no releases. The MIT LICENSE also credits Farza's Clicky, the upstream fork source; bundled Neko sprites carry a BSD-2-Clause file.

OpenMobile pipeline for AndroidWorld: random-walk exploration, memory-based task-instruction synthesis, learner/expert policy-switching rollouts, conversion to LLaMA-Factory SFT data, and AndroidWorld evaluation.

Recorded specifications: {"availability": "Public synthesis, rollout, conversion and evaluation code with LLaMA-Factory configs; the OpenMobile-8B checkpoint and OpenMobile-Data are released separately on Hugging Face.", "repository_revision": "faca68f386aff7277cdf494c84693c51090229c6"}

Official code of the OpenMobile paper (COLM 2026 per the README). AndroidWorld/ holds a modified AndroidWorld copy with exploration (random_walk_aw.py), rollout (run_diy.py), post-processing and evaluation scripts; task_synthesis/ builds screen context and environment memory and generates and judges instructions with a strong multimodal model; LlamaFactory/ registers the four released data splits and gives Qwen3-VL and Qwen3.5 SFT configs. The tree also contains an Android-Lab folder. The Qwen3VL agent in AndroidWorld/android_world/agents/seeact_v.py sends recent plain screenshots to an OpenAI-compatible endpoint and executes the returned mobile_use tool calls; UI-element metadata is saved for post-processing only. The policy-switching mode lets a strong model monitor a weaker actor and take over. The README's AndroidWorld success rates include Qwen3.5-9B results it identifies as unreproducible under vLLM.

Recorded specifications: {"availability": "Public Electron source with tagged releases; local BYOK mode needs no account, while hosted models, connectors and team features use OOMOL services.", "repository_revision": "d568845ea03f6bae3b1cef2d80b19b5b32bc7952"}

Recorded as adjacent: Wanta is a general agent host whose local tools are files, shell, skills, knowledge and SaaS connectors (OpenConnector), and its only graphical executor is the integrated browser. The Electron main process owns a WebContentsView per task page, Playwright attaches through a custom CDP transport over webContents.debugger, and an authenticated loopback bridge serves seven OpenCode tools: browser_navigate, browser_read (title, URL, dialog state and a Playwright AI-mode ARIA snapshot with refs), browser_click and browser_type on refs or unique selectors, browser_scroll, browser_screenshot and browser_dialog. The user shares the page and completes logins and CAPTCHAs; in Default Access the agent is told to hand sensitive actions to the user, which the design document calls a behavioural policy rather than a system guarantee. External agents keep their own accounts; hosted models, connectors and team workspaces need an OOMOL account. Packages for macOS, Windows and Linux. Root LICENSE is Apache-2.0.

Recorded specifications: {"availability": "Public source for the Chromium patches, the assistant extension and the agent library; building the browser requires a Chromium checkout and depot_tools, and no releases are published.", "repository_revision": "b04fcf631fe67ddf7ab6d54f6388635d16f468f9"}

Three parts: chromium/ holds a patch list and scripts that rebrand a separately checked-out Chromium source tree with the root branding_assets/ and load the assistant as a built-in component extension in a side panel (no prebuilt browser is released); chromium-extension/ is that assistant (sidebar chat, options, background agent); packages/core is the TypeScript agent library with planning, replanning, a chat agent, MCP clients, memory compression and web search. Its browser agent injects a DOM-tree script that indexes clickable elements as pseudo-HTML and, in the default normal mode with draw marking, sends a viewport capture with the indexed boxes drawn on it; tools navigate, click, type, scroll, hover, select options, extract page content and switch tabs, and the extension executes them through chrome.tabs, chrome.scripting and chrome.debugger. Electron app (desktop/) that starts a local Next.js server (app/, lib/server/) on port 3210; version 0.0.28 in package.json, matching release tag v0.0.28 at 92ec73d, and the inspected commit 62c7f98 is later. Bots' tasks run on Orgo cloud computers launched from the bops-base template that orgo/bops-base.mjs builds from vm/ (Codex, the screen MCP and per-screen Chrome helpers). By default lib/server/computer-task.ts runs each thread on OpenAI's Responses API computer tool: Orgo's API returns a screenshot of the bot's screen, and every click, double-click, drag, scroll, typing or key press the model asks for is executed as xdotool commands through Orgo's bash endpoint, with the result screen sent back; the same loop offers a page_script tool that runs a short Playwright script on the screen's Chrome over CDP, a Linux shell, web search, a password vault and app, data and CRM tools. With BOPS_COMPUTER_TOOL=0 threads use OpenAI's Agents API with Codex and vm/screen_mcp.py, which exposes one screen's screenshot and input actions over MCP. Tasks on the user's own Mac run in a bot-owned Chrome; with Full access they also get a shell and the user's apps through Cua Driver behind vm/mac-ui-mcp.mjs, which hides sensitive apps, sends input only in the background and blocks quitting, copying and pasting (lib/server/local.ts). Per the README, reading runs at once while sending, creating and paying wait for the user's approval, and any screen can be watched live and taken over. Self-hosting requires an Orgo account and two OpenAI API keys, with Honcho, Composio, treg, AgentMail, AgentPhone and TypeSafe recommended or optional; signing in with Orgo instead routes provider calls through Orgo's hosted Bops Cloud (cloud/). Licensed FSL-1.1-ALv2 (fair source; competing products and hosted services are excluded, and each version becomes Apache-2.0 two years after release); components/message-ui/ is adapted from MIT-licensed code.

Published by Outcrawl; the GitHub description calls the repository an automatic mirror of Outcrawl's production repository. Packages: scout (entry point), runtime (agent loop), model (prompts and provider-neutral clients), scout-core, scout-cdp (DevTools-protocol driver) and agenthands (local pointer and keyboard planning). It runs against a local browser, any CDP endpoint or Outcrawl's hosted browser, which needs an Outcrawl key and adds residential connections, captcha solving and replays. The README reports 92.5% page reach on Browser Use's 80-site benchmark. Root code is Apache-2.0; packages/agenthands keeps its own MIT license.

Gemini Browser Agent
Resource type: agent

Chrome extension and Python WebSocket bridge that run Gemini 2.5 Computer Use on the user's active tab, sending tab screenshots to the model and executing its clicks, typing and scrolling via content scripts.

Recorded specifications: {"availability": "Public Python bridge and unpacked Chrome extension source without a license file; it calls Google's hosted Gemini 2.5 Computer Use preview model with the user's own API key and bundles no model.", "license_review": {"code": {"evidence_urls": ["https://api.github.com/repos/pmbstyle/gemini-browser-agent/git/trees/540b6fd7f1bfcfc351b2f7139ea4404cb089472f?recursive=1"], "reason": "The inspected recursive tree has no license file and the README names no license; source terms remain unknown."}}, "repository_revision": "540b6fd7f1bfcfc351b2f7139ea4404cb089472f"}

The README calls the project a research experiment and scaffolding. websocket_agent.py is a local WebSocket server that calls gemini-2.5-computer-use-preview-10-2025 through google-genai with the browser computer-use environment; widget/ is an unpacked Manifest V3 extension with a side panel where the user connects to the bridge and enters a goal. Each turn the extension captures the visible tab with chrome.tabs.captureVisibleTab, the bridge converts the model's 0-1000 normalized coordinates to viewport pixels, and the extension carries out clicks, typing, key presses, hovering, scrolling and navigation by injecting functions (chrome.scripting.executeScript) that dispatch synthetic DOM events at document.elementFromPoint. Drag and drop is approximated with mousedown and mouseup events, unhandled model actions return an unimplemented warning, and the side panel sets a step limit (default 10). It needs a Gemini API key and acts in the user's own browser without a sandbox; the README points to the author's separate gemini-computer-use repository for sandboxed runs. The repository has no license file at the inspected commit.

Recorded specifications: {"availability": "Public MIT Python source and a prebuilt macOS app; it needs an Anthropic or OpenAI agent runtime and bundles no model.", "repository_revision": "0d5e9d3168cdde02d43448fa4a80521ebac3501d"}

Requires macOS 13 or newer, Python 3.12 and Accessibility, Screen Recording and Input Monitoring permissions; Windows support remains pending. The recorder (pynput listeners and mss screenshots) writes a manifest of clicks, typing, hotkeys and scrolls with pre-action screenshots, plus optional extract and detail notes. Reflection turns the trace into a coordinate-free schema.json; an optimizer writes optimized_plan.json, preferring script steps, then browser_harness steps (Chrome CDP through a browser-harness git submodule), then ui_agent steps; a build agent packages a Claude Skill-compatible folder with run.sh, inputs and a fallback plan. The ui_agent drives the Mac in the foreground through cua-computer-server MCP tools, which AI Mime extends with combined screenshot-plus-accessibility-tree reads, and is told to target accessibility elements before screenshot coordinates. Agent runtimes are Anthropic (Claude Code) or OpenAI (Codex), selected during onboarding, with custom providers in user_config.yml. A prebuilt macOS DMG is linked from the README.

The README presents it as a Smart India Hackathon entry for problem statement 26171, whose listed organisation is ISRO. The Manifest V3 extension (version 1.31.0 at review) is loaded unpacked in Chrome; the README says Firefox has been built from the same source since v1.17.0. src/content/dom-detector.js paints numbered boxes on interactive elements, and the service worker captures the tab through the Chrome debugger or captureVisibleTab, so screenshots carry those marks. In privacy mode, MediaPipe, YOLO, ViT, Tesseract OCR and regex/checksum PII detectors run in the browser, and src/lib/privacy-firewall.js blocks or blanks a frame when sanitizing fails. Actions use selectors, with debugger Input.dispatchMouseEvent clicks where needed, inside a tab-group sandbox with an approval mode. Models: on-device Gemma 4, cloud providers, or Ollama through the bundled server. OpenCometBench is the repository's own test suite; its PII precision/recall uses a synthetic corpus built from the detector's own rules, as the README states, leaving independence outside the measurement.

The repository holds the harness-bench CLI (harness x model x task matrix expansion with credential gating, run, batch and a leaderboard renderer over ClawBench result summaries), six harness adapters (openclaw, hermes, claw-code, browser-use, stagehand, coze-studio), each a Dockerfile, setup script and run script built on the clawbench-base image, and a one-task smoke fixture. The tasks, the five-layer recording and the judge belong to ClawBench; this repository holds the harness, whose run and batch commands call clawbench.run_case and require clawbench-eval 0.2.0 or later. At the inspected commit the README's fixtures/lite.txt 20-task subset is absent from the tree, the browser-use run script calls a run-browser-use.py that neither the tree nor its Dockerfile supplies, and the leaderboard and demo videos are placeholders. stagehand and coze-studio need BrowserBase or Coze credentials.

Built by @RichardHruby and @jesse-olympus at Anon as a Next.js app. Each step sends a JPEG screenshot and form-relevant HTML (walking into shadow roots) to claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929, which returns one of six typed screen states (credential_login_form, choice_screen, magic_login_link, loading_screen, blocked_screen, logged_in_screen) with Playwright locators; locators unresolved in the live DOM are fed back for up to three analysis attempts. Browsers are Browserbase sessions reached over CDP, so Anthropic and Browserbase keys are required. The user supplies credentials, choices and magic links through the chat UI, and Playwright types or clicks them. package.json is a private app (login-machine 0.1.0); a hosted demo is linked from the README.

Resource type: framework

Official ScreenParse code: the Webshot toolkit that renders websites with Playwright, records visible DOM elements as boxed, nested annotations, relabels them with Qwen3-VL, exports YOLO data and evaluates parsers.
Platforms: web
Topics: screen-understanding, data-generation, evaluation

Recorded specifications: {"availability": "Public Webshot generation, refinement, export, YOLO training and evaluation source; the dataset and the ScreenVLM and ScreenParser checkpoints are separate Hugging Face releases.", "repository_revision": "b294659b87fb75f3fd4964310fd2039d385749b3", "repository_tree_sha": "7643cfa0696153a9173be8a2a9070250b4b761d8"}

The README calls this the official code release for the ICML 2026 paper and links the ScreenParse dataset and the ScreenVLM and ScreenParser checkpoints on Hugging Face; none of them is stored in this repository, and the only training script, scripts/train.py, trains Ultralytics YOLO detectors. At commit b294659b, webshot/src/webshot/worker.py drives Chromium through Playwright, dismisses cookie banners and overlays, and records each visible DOM element's tag, role, attributes, text, bounding rectangle and parent and child indices with a screenshot; vlm_refine.py and vlm_quality_score.py relabel elements and score annotation quality with Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct by default through vLLM. The evaluation CLI runs YOLO, RT-DETR, OmniParser weights, Qwen3-VL, InternVL3, Gemini, PaddleOCR-VL and ScreenVLM on YOLO-format, GroundCUA or ScreenSpot data and reports PageIoU, label PageIoU, mAP, recall and NED. The Webshot README reports 771K screenshots and 21M elements for the dataset. MIT covers this code only; dataset and checkpoint terms are declared on their own Hub pages.

macOS voice and typed computer-use app that walks the front app's Accessibility tree, has the hosted Jev model pick an operation and a numbered target each step, and acts via Accessibility actions and synthetic input.

Recorded specifications: {"availability": "Public Swift source built locally with build.sh; decisions require a TypeSafe API key for the hosted Jev model, and planning optionally an OpenRouter key.", "repository_revision": "b22e568adf110eeb64f89bf4d731a69d23c461dc"}

The Swift app (built as Desktop Voice.app; macOS 14.2+ and Xcode) reads the front window's Accessibility tree, skipping secure text fields, and sends the command, app and window names, numbered targets and recent actions to TypeSafe's hosted systemone endpoint with model jev-latest; no screenshots are sent (Sources/JevDesktop/Desktop.swift, Sources/JevCore/Decision.swift). Actions use Accessibility presses and value setting plus CGEvent mouse, key and scroll events. An optional OpenRouter key enables a planner model (default inception/mercury-2.5) that splits a spoken command into steps; Jev still chooses each on-screen target (Sources/JevCore/Planner.swift). Input is Apple Speech hold-to-talk, hands-free mode, an optional "Hey Jev" wake phrase, or typed commands. The README says low-confidence and destructive picks stop and ask. Jev is a hosted model.

Recorded specifications: {"availability": "Public source with tagged GitHub releases; runs locally with Node.js and Docker, using the owner's model API keys.", "package_version": "0.4.1", "release_tag": "v0.4.1", "repository_revision": "489e9c4fa4c3705c4ff87d1f90e7d8b616837c14"}

Next.js app run locally (version 0.4.1 in package.json; tag v0.4.1 points at b8016b5, and the inspected commit 489e9c4 is later). Each agent's workstation is a Docker container built from workstation/: Debian (trixie-slim) with Xvfb, xfwm4 and a panel, Chromium, x11vnc and noVNC, xdotool and scrot, a persistent home volume, and an inactivity watchdog. lib/agent/tools.ts defines the tool belt for the Vercel AI SDK streamText loop: shell and fs_* through docker exec; screen_capture and screen_share (scrot JPEG through xiryn-shot); pointer_click, pointer_move, pointer_drag, pointer_scroll, key_type and key_press (xdotool in lib/workstation.ts), each returning a fresh screenshot; request_takeover; vault_list, vault_fill, request_payment_approval and request_secret; memory_write and memory_forget; web_search and web_fetch through Firecrawl; and delegate for squads. Observation is plain screenshots of a 1280x800 display with pixel coordinates; there is no accessibility tree or element annotation. Before each step the runtime keeps only the two most recent screenshots in full (docs/architecture.md). The vault fills saved logins and cards into fields without the model seeing them, and cards only after the owner approves the payment. The user can watch and take over the desktop, and the agent hands over at logins, payments, one-time codes or CAPTCHAs, with a Telegram notice when paired. Models come from the owner's keys for OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI, Groq, Mistral, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, Ollama, LM Studio or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. The README's comparison with hosted agents is the author's own. Root LICENSE is MIT.

System1-Agents
Resource type: framework
Review status: curated
Scope: adjacent

Framework that puts System 1 decision models such as Jev, Laya or Cua-S1 in openJiuwen agents to pick one typed option per step; ships browser, desktop-app, game, ALFWorld and ticket-routing agents.
Platforms: web, desktop, windows, macos
Topics: efficiency, action-prediction, web-navigation

Recorded specifications: {"availability": "Public Python source with CLI, MCP server and agent skills; decision models need a TypeSafe or OpenRouter key, a served endpoint, or the optional Cua-S1 extra.", "repository_revision": "0fe20f5044d455126c81f668ac9d28d706e6d3c0", "repository_tree_sha": "f252f9febcc8edd96b8fdd81664500be72c0b33f"}

Adjacent because browser and desktop control are two of several shipped domains; the package (s1a) is equally aimed at games, ALFWorld, ticket routing and an injection-guard rail. On a decision turn the System 1 model answers typed choice questions while a chat model keeps planning, typed values and the final answer. The browser front runs a stock openJiuwen browser subagent (pinned ThinkFlowLab fork of agent-core) over @playwright/mcp; its in-page probe numbers the visible controls of the top document's light DOM, and the decision model chooses an element plus an operation head (CLICK, TYPE_TEXT, PRESS_ENTER, SELECT, scrolling). OmniJev instead receives a page screenshot. The desktop agent drives a Windows or macOS app window through the external Cua Driver over MCP, clicking accessibility elements bound to a window snapshot. Decision models are reached through TypeSafe, OpenRouter or served endpoints; Cua-S1 Nano runs in process from a pinned trycua/cua subdirectory. Speed and cost tables in the README are the publisher's single-episode comparisons. The browser files carry Huawei copyright notices with ThinkFlowLab modifications under Apache-2.0.

The demo model has 1.8M parameters and was trained from scratch by behavioural cloning to compute simple additions and subtractions of up to two-digit numbers in an open GNOME Calculator window on Ubuntu at 1920x1080; the README says it is brittle to new backgrounds, resolutions or other windows. In the demo runner each step grabs the full screen with PIL ImageGrab, resizes it to the configured 1024x576 input, and clicks the predicted position with pyautogui until the model predicts end. Neither the trained checkpoint (run.py expects data/gnome_calculator_model/epoch=14-step=1875.ckpt) nor the demonstration recordings (the data module reads screen.mp4 and events.jsonl under data/screen_recordings/) are in the repository; the README instead offers a VirtualBox VM image, whose HTTP HEAD response on 2026-10-18 reported 23,411,565,568 bytes, last modified 2023-10-11. Coding is the primary purpose: the README frames release v0.0.1 (Apple Silicon, macOS 13 or later, locally signed and not notarized) around a describe, investigate, edit, review and verify loop, and calls browser and desktop automation experimental. server.mjs runs an eido-browser MCP server with browser_* tools. Its default Ultrafast engine, adapted in TypeScript from browser-use/jev-ultrafast, launches Playwright Chromium, injects snapshot.js to list up to 250 visible interactive elements with roles and labels plus visible page text, has a decision model choose one click, fill, select, scroll or wait step at a time, and dispatches mouse and key events over the DevTools protocol (browser.ts); per server.mjs, screenshots serve recording and the inspector, with model input drawn from the page listing. config.mjs points decision requests at the hosted TypeSafe API (model jev-latest) by default and, unless overridden, generates typed text with the user's main model. A Legacy engine uses the jev-browser npm dependency. computer.mjs registers the bundled or a user-installed cua-driver as the eido_computer MCP server, which needs macOS Accessibility and Screen Recording permission; native/cua/upstream.json pins trycua/cua tag cua-driver-rs-v0.34.0, and per NOTICE the native/cua/overlay patches add session-owned background focus, exact-window keyboard guards and window capture validation. NOTICE licenses Eido-original code GPL-3.0-or-later, while Zed components marked Apache-2.0, the Cua Driver and jev-ultrafast-derived code (MIT), pi (MIT) and upstream pi-acp adapter code (Apache-2.0) keep their own terms.

Recorded specifications: {"availability": "Public Kotlin source and APK releases on main; no model weights.", "repository_revision": "c8a6d7f03422eb01744b01f3ee77bf7757741f7e", "repository_tree_sha": "30aed2ffc589b88d571309a02396b6ea8a1c42ea"}

Kotlin Android app (minimum SDK 26) published by Turbo1123. Shizuku gives it ADB-level shell access without root, which DeviceController.kt uses for screencap, input tap/swipe/text and am start; the agent's floating overlay is hidden while each plain screenshot is taken. In the default mode MobileAgent.kt runs Manager (plan), Executor (one of click, double_tap, long_press, type, swipe, system_button, open_app, wait, take_over or answer, with pixel coordinates), ActionReflector (compares the before and after screenshots) and an optional Notetaker over an OpenAI-compatible VLM API, for at most 25 steps by default; the README calls this layer a Kotlin port of Mobile-Agent-v3. Two other modes call GUI-Owl through Alibaba Cloud DashScope's GUI agent endpoint (default model pre-gui_owl_7b), which returns actions directly, or an OpenAI-compatible MAI-UI server (default localhost:8000, MAI-UI-2B) with MAI-UI's prompt format and up to three history screenshots. A Skills layer (app/src/main/assets/skills.json) can instead hand a request to another app through a deep link, and Tools cover app search, deep links, clipboard, shell and HTTP. When screencap is blocked on a secure screen the agent asks the user before continuing; the Manager prompt stops the run when a screen actively asks for payment confirmation, a password or biometric verification, and the Executor can hand logins and captchas to the user (take_over) or ask for confirmation of payment actions. The README says a 2.0 version based on AccessibilityService is developed on a separate branch; this record describes main. Root LICENSE is MIT; latest release V1.4.2.

Browser Agent (uiuing)
Resource type: agent
Review status: curated

Chrome side-panel agent whose page engine reads a whole-page semantic DOM snapshot, re-grounds targets by element fingerprints, dispatches DOM events and checks post-conditions before reporting success.

Recorded specifications: {"availability": "Source and a packaged Chrome extension zip in GitHub releases", "release_tag": "v0.0.1", "repository_revision": "a8517e2c5cd5be9d77e66f90180e25490c67d9ba"}

Chrome Manifest V3 extension by uiuing, first released as v0.0.1 (Chrome zip in GitHub releases). The model acts on pages only through the page_act tool, which hands a goal to an engine that builds a semantic snapshot of DOM nodes with roles, accessible names, values, occlusion, open shadow roots and same-origin iframes (packages/extension/src/engine/page/perception.ts), resolves targets by fingerprint against a fresh snapshot and fires click, input, change and key events in the page (engine/page/execute.ts). The page_screenshot tool shows a capture to the user; its description limits the model to other page information rather than the pixels (tools/page.ts). A chrome.debugger channel is used for file uploads and falls back to DOM synthesis. Tools carry read, act or dangerous risk tiers with site allow/block lists and confirmation; verified runs can be saved as skills and replayed over batch rows. Model ports cover OpenAI-compatible, OpenAI Responses and Anthropic APIs. The docs/benchmark.md comparison is publisher-run on the project's own fixtures against its own replica of a viewport-only baseline.

text:
Webagent (webagent.cloud)
Resource type: agent
Review status: curated
Scope: core

Self-hostable browser-agent server that runs Browser Use or Notte agents, turns a run's recorded actions into a parameterized workflow, and replays it with Playwright, falling back to the agent when a step fails.
Recorded aliases: webagent
Platforms: web
Topics: automation, workflow, web-navigation

Recorded specifications: {"availability": "Public server, workflow replay code, React UI and Dockerfile; no release or tag.", "repository_revision": "21969388bbb70a0ebf44aee0a8a913ccc54d294e", "repository_tree_sha": "83f267d148ba5eb8061d32bb2e2c77bae8043328"}

Open-source code of the webagent.cloud hosted service, published by webagent-cloud. A FastAPI server (server.py, webagent/api.py) with a bundled React UI accepts a prompt and runs it with the engine set by ENGINE_PROVIDER: Browser Use by default, or Notte, whose agent is fixed to gemini-2.5-flash with at most 30 steps. The browser comes from BROWSER_PROVIDER: a local Playwright Chromium over CDP, Browserbase or Steel; at the reviewed commit the Steel provider's create_session takes a context argument that the caller omits. Models are reached through Browser Use's chat clients for OpenAI, DeepSeek, Anthropic, Google and Groq; other provider values fall back to the OpenAI client. After a run, workflow_builder_service.py asks an LLM to extract parameters from the prompt and template the recorded actions with their element XPaths; workflow_replay_service.py replays those steps with Playwright (navigation, search, XPath clicks and typing, scrolling, key presses, uploads, dropdowns) without a model and, when an action fails, hands that step to the AI engine for up to three attempts. Tasks, runs and results are kept in a local SQLite database; results can be text or JSON validated against a supplied JSON Schema, and a webhook can be called on completion. The README's n8n, Zapier and Make integrations and Stagehand engine are not in the tree. Root LICENSE is MIT.

Catalog record: https://awesomecua.com/resources/github-webagent-cloud-webagent/

Adjacent: the app's main job is hosting DeepSeek Harness (DSH), a coding-agent runtime, on Android 10+ ARM64 without root or Termux, alongside a terminal and file manager; the GUI executors are bundled tools that DSH chooses between. The README declares GPL v3 for the project; pilot/NOTICE marks interlock-relay-core as Apache-2.0 and the DSHBox adapter as GPL-3.0, and PRoot, Debian and other components keep their own terms. WebDroid Agent
Resource type: agent
Review status: curated
Scope: core

Browser-hosted Android phone agent that connects over WebUSB/WebADB, sends screenshots plus a uiautomator text tree to an OpenAI-compatible or Gemini vision model, and runs its JSON actions through ADB.
Recorded aliases: github:yeahhe365/webadb-autoglm, yeahhe365/webadb-autoglm, https://github.com/yeahhe365/webadb-autoglm
Platforms: android
Topics: mobile-navigation, human-in-the-loop, automation

Recorded specifications: {"availability": "Source; static web deployment or Docker image build; GitHub releases", "release_tag": "v0.2.0", "repository_revision": "6ef50805d0f4509d7222dd269d8e329ab95ec902"}

A React app that runs entirely in a Chromium browser (WebUSB through Tango/WebADB), or in Docker with a local proxy for model requests; the browser is the controller and the operated surface is a USB-connected Android device. Each step captures screencap output and, best effort, a compressed uiautomator dump of visible text, IDs, clickable state and bounds (src/lib/contextBuilder.ts); actions use pixel or 0-1000 normalized coordinates and become adb input, am start and keyboard-broadcast commands (src/adapters/inputCommands.ts). Sensitive taps can require confirmation, take_over hands control back to the user and type_secret sends the model only a secret ID; an unrestricted mode skips these checks. README.md is in Chinese and README.en-US.md is the English version. The repository was renamed from yeahhe365/webadb-autoglm (same repository ID 1244747615).

AutoGUI code
Resource type: framework
Review status: curated
Scope: core

AutoGUI's functionality-annotation pipeline (collect, reject, annotate from accessibility-tree changes, verify, generate tasks), with Qwen-VL LoRA fine-tuning and lmms-eval-based grounding evaluation.
Recorded aliases: github:bravegroup/autogui, BraveGroup/AutoGUI, https://github.com/BraveGroup/AutoGUI
Platforms: web, android
Topics: grounding, data-generation, screen-understanding

Recorded specifications: {"availability": "Public annotation pipeline, fine-tuning and evaluation code; the training data and checkpoint are on the Hub and the FuncPred test split is on Google Drive.", "repository_revision": "0c28fd248ec66623cd7f7b00275e229f4bec9bf3"}

Official AutoGUI code. autogui_anno/ is a self-contained reimplementation of the paper's web and mobile annotation pipeline: it gathers screenshots and accessibility trees, rejects unpredictable elements, has an OpenAI-compatible LLM describe each element's function from before/after accessibility-tree changes, verifies descriptions by re-grounding them, and composes grounding tasks at several image scales; web collection uses Playwright. finetune/ trains Qwen-VL-Chat with LoRA on the released AutoGUI training data, and the adapted lmms_eval package runs FuncPred, ScreenSpot, ScreenSpot-v2, RefExp, MOTIF and VisualWebBench grounding tasks for models the README lists, including Qwen-VL-Chat, Qwen2-VL, LLaVA, CogAgent, Ferret-UI, UGround and OS-Atlas. The README links the 702K training set on the Hub, a 2K FuncPred test split on Google Drive and an AutoGUI-Qwen checkpoint. The arXiv abstract points to autogui-project.github.io, the repository's homepage, which links this code; that page's own Paper link points to an unrelated arXiv ID. The README's clone command uses the former BraveGroup/AutoGUI address.

Research code by Zora Zhiruo Wang and coauthors. The agent (asi/agent.py) observes BrowserGym pages through the flattened accessibility tree by default, with HTML and screenshot inputs as options, and acts through BrowserGym's action set. run_online.py alternates solving WebArena tasks, judging the trajectory with the autoeval LLM evaluator, inducing website-specific skill functions (asi/induce/induce_actions.py) and testing them before they are added; the README also runs AWM and vanilla baselines from the same script. The repository vendors a copy of BrowserGym packages (browsergym/, Apache-2.0 per their pyproject files) and expects self-hosted WebArena sites. The root LICENSE is CC BY-SA 4.0. Webfuse
Resource type: product
Review status: curated
Scope: core

Web augmentation proxy that serves a site inside the user's browser and lets AI agents read DOM, screenshot or accessibility-tree snapshots and click, type or scroll through an automation API and a session MCP server.
Platforms: web
Topics: web-navigation, automation

Recorded specifications: {"access": "publisher-managed", "pricing_url": "https://www.webfuse.com/pricing"}

Webfuse serves an existing website through a configurable proxy session and injects Extensions on the client side without changes to the site's code. Its Automation API, callable from an Extension, provides perception (DOM snapshot, Base64 screenshot of the page, accessibility tree, text selection) and actuation (click, type, scroll, select, key press, mouse move, text selection), targeting an element, CSS selector, point coordinate or Webfuse element ID across shadow DOM and iframes; the screenshot method is documented for Chromium-based browsers only. The Session MCP Server exposes the same tools, plus navigate and page info, to MCP clients authenticated with a Space automation key. tool.applyD2Snap() applies the DOM downsampling method of arXiv 2508.04412, whose second author, Nicholas Piël, is named on the about page as Webfuse's CEO and founder; the about page also says Webfuse grew out of the team's Surfly session technology. The pricing page lists Spark and Forge monthly plans metered in virtual minutes, a custom Foundry tier and a 14-day free trial.

Primary source: https://www.webfuse.com
Catalog record: https://awesomecua.com/resources/url-255e1ea24461c1f205eb/

Predicate Systems (formerly SentienceAPI)
Resource type: product
Review status: curated
Scope: core

Runtime trust layer for browser agents: a sidecar checks each action against local policy before it runs, and SDKs turn pages into compact ranked element snapshots and verify outcomes with DOM assertions.
Recorded aliases: SentienceAPI, Sentience API
Platforms: web
Topics: web-navigation, safety-security, state-tracking, observability, efficiency

Recorded specifications: {"access": "publisher-managed"}

Predicate Systems Inc. was formerly SentienceAPI; www.sentienceapi.com redirects to this site. It has three parts. Predicate Authority is a Rust sidecar that evaluates local YAML policies and issues signed mandates before an action executes. Predicate Runtime, with Python and TypeScript SDKs, collects element geometry through a browser extension, gives the model a structured snapshot of element IDs, roles, text, importance scores and boxes (about 0.6-1.2k tokens per step by the publisher's estimate), executes the chosen action and runs assertions such as url_contains or exists; it runs standalone with Playwright or under browser-use, and an optional Gateway reranks elements with ONNX models. predicate-secure wraps frameworks such as browser-use, Playwright and LangChain with both checks. The documentation also covers Predicate Studio traces and Predicate Vault. New accounts start with 100 free credits.

Primary source: https://predicatesystems.ai

Free Mode includes supported models and cloud browser time with sponsored cards and a daily allowance; users can bring their own model keys, and schedules, triggers, Cookie Sync and API or MCP control of the user's own Chrome require a paid plan. Recordings capture DOM interactions and the page's own network calls in place of screen recordings, and can be turned into replays or into subroutines that call a site's endpoints directly. An experimental Jev option lets a separate model choose browser actions while the selected model plans. The company also offers Rover, an agent that site owners embed for their visitors, and sells browser-agent trajectories and replica business apps for evaluation. The documentation says the Recursion agent executes each plain-language instruction on the web page in real time and adds the matching blocks to a workflow; Action blocks click, type, press keys and refresh, go back or open, close and switch tabs, alongside navigation, extraction, checkpoint (natural-language assertion), for-loop and conditional blocks. Action and navigation blocks cache the elements or URLs they used and fall back to full reasoning when a cached step fails. A deployed agent gets synchronous and asynchronous API endpoints. The benchmarks page reports 87.0% on 602 of WebVoyager's 643 tasks (41 removed as impossible, booking, login or print tasks) and 90% against 56% for Anthropic's computer-use demo on 50 sampled tasks, for a hierarchical agent of planners, an executor and critics that runs mainly on GPT-4o; these figures are publisher-reported.

Twin Labs SAS, a Paris company, provides the service under its terms. Agents prefer APIs and built-in tools; the Web Agent takes over only when no API, or no API scope, covers a step, and the documentation calls it the most expensive and least reliable execution mode. It runs in an embedded browser on an isolated cloud computer dedicated to the agent. Reviewed against the ICLR 2026 proceedings page and abstract, the full proceedings PDF and the platform README at commit 4536036; the OpenReview forum lists it as an ICLR 2026 Poster. Two anonymized agents run the same user-written instruction in parallel, identically initialized Ubuntu or Windows virtual machines on AWS EC2, shown to users through a browser VNC view and synchronized replays; the paper turns the pairwise votes into a Bradley-Terry ranking and also collects optional step-level labels. It reports 2,201 filtered votes from 1,058 users over 12 agents, compares pure GUI agents with agents that also call tools or write code, and links github.com/xlang-ai/computer-agent-arena for the platform and a Hugging Face page for the collected data; neither release was reviewed here. No arXiv version was found.

Trains a separate language model to rewrite lengthy web page observations into focused descriptions for LLM web agents, keeping training targets that let several LLMs predict the correct next action.

Published: 2025-05-01

Publication source: https://openreview.net/forum?id=3Gzz7ZQLiz

Reviewed against the ICLR 2025 proceedings page and PDF; the OpenReview forum lists it as an ICLR 2025 Poster. LCoW's contextualization module reads the task, previous actions and a raw page observation such as an accessibility tree, and is retrained each iteration by supervised fine-tuning on the sampled rewrites that let several LLM agents recover the ground-truth action in successful trajectories. Appendix B fine-tunes Phi-3-mini-Instruct for WebShop and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct for WorkArena and WebArena. WebShop and WorkArena are the main benchmarks; a 165-task WebArena subset tests generalization to unseen task types. The same paper is posted on arXiv as 2503.10689 with the comment "Accepted to ICLR 2025". The paper points to lcowiclr2025.github.io for code.

Gumloop
Resource type: product

Business agent platform whose agents work through app connectors and can turn on a Chromium browser that clicks, types, signs in with saved logins and hands control to a person when a site needs it.
Platforms: web

Recorded specifications: {"access": "publisher-managed", "pricing_url": "https://www.gumloop.com/pricing"}

Recorded as adjacent: Gumloop presents itself as a platform for building, sharing and running AI agents for business teams, which work mainly through app connectors, MCP servers and APIs, and its help pages advise using the agent browser only when no connector or API covers a task. The agent browser is an ability turned on per custom agent, and on Enterprise organizations it is off by default until an admin adds it to a role. It runs Chromium on the agent's computer, which shares the agent's code sandbox, and opens pages, clicks, types, scrolls and switches tabs. Gumloop types saved logins and 2FA codes for the agent without showing them to the model, keeps sign-ins in browser profiles, offers residential proxies and desktop or Pixel 7 mobile emulation, and pauses to hand the live browser to a person at logins, CAPTCHAs or purchase confirmations. Every browser step is recorded for replay. Agents can also be reached from Slack, Microsoft Teams, email and text messages.

Ace
Resource type: product
Review status: curated
Scope: core

General Agents' desktop autopilot, trained on recorded expert behavior, that predicts clicks, keystrokes and other actions from screenshots; its API client ships a macOS controller that executes them.
Recorded aliases: General Agents Ace
Platforms: desktop, macos
Topics: automation, grounding, imitation-learning

Recorded specifications: {"availability": "Hosted models reached through an API; the API and documentation hosts had DNS resolution failures at review time, and pricing and sign-up paths remain unpublished."}

The Ace page describes a computer autopilot that uses the mouse and keyboard on the user's desktop, says it was trained by software specialists and domain experts on over a million tasks, and charts publisher figures for click-prediction accuracy for ace-control-medium and ace-control-small against Operator, Claude 3.7 Sonnet, UI-TARS-72B-SFT and other models, plus action latency. The About page says Ace learns from experts' screen recordings with mouse and keyboard logs, and that General Agents is developing video-language-action models. The official Python client (generalagents-python 0.1.1 at commit d36f6a8) posts a WebP screenshot, the instruction and recent actions to /v1/control/predict on api.generalagents.com; its macOS Computer class captures the screen with screencapture and performs clicks, drags, scrolls, key presses and typing through pyautogui. The client's Apache-2.0 code license does not cover the hosted models. At review time api.generalagents.com and docs.generalagents.com had DNS resolution failures; the reviewed pages leave pricing, download and sign-up paths unspecified, so current availability remains unknown.

Firecrawl
Resource type: product
Review status: curated
Scope: adjacent

Hosted web data API for AI agents that searches and scrapes pages into Markdown or JSON, with an Interact endpoint and browser sandbox in which prompts or Playwright code click, type and fill forms.
Platforms: web
Topics: web-navigation, sandbox, automation

Recorded specifications: {"access": "publisher-managed", "pricing_url": "https://www.firecrawl.dev/pricing"}

Recorded as adjacent: the publisher presents Firecrawl as a web data API for AI agents, and its search, scrape, map and crawl endpoints return page content as Markdown, HTML, JSON or screenshots without operating the page. Interact continues from a scrape result: POST /v2/scrape/{scrapeId}/interact takes either a natural-language prompt, which it carries out by clicking, typing and scrolling, or Playwright code, and returns a CDP URL and live-view URLs; named profiles keep browser state such as logins between sessions. The Browser Sandbox (POST /v2/interact) opens a standalone isolated browser session with Playwright and the agent-browser CLI preinstalled, CDP access and an embeddable interactive live view. The /agent endpoint gathers data from a prompt by searching and navigating sites and runs on the publisher's Spark 2 model. The homepage HTML changes on every request, so the primary receipt is the documentation introduction. The homepage also links the repository github.com/firecrawl/firecrawl; which hosted features that code includes was not reviewed, and its license does not cover the hosted service.

Primary source: https://www.firecrawl.dev

text:
In-Context Teacher–Student Guidance for Open-Weight Browser Agents
Resource type: paper
Review status: curated
Scope: core

Training-free protocol that turns a teacher model's offline reasoning traces into prompt guidance for open-weight browser agents; on MiniWoB++ it lifts solved student-task pairs from 208 to 271 across ten students.
Platforms: web
Topics: web-navigation, training-free, efficiency
Published: 2026-10-19
Authors: Wéwerthon Silva Cardoso, Ricardo Marcacini

Publication edition: In-Context Teacher–Student Guidance for Open-Weight Browser Agents
Publication authors: Wéwerthon Silva Cardoso, Ricardo Marcacini
Publication edition date (recorded precision): 2026-10-19
Publication venue: Anais do XIV Symposium on Knowledge Discovery, Mining and Learning (KDMiLe 2026)
Publication publisher: Sociedade Brasileira de Computação - SBC
Publication pages: 121-128
Publication doi: 10.5753/kdmile.2026.32021
Publication date basis: Crossref metadata deposited for the DOI gives issued and published-online dates of 2026-10-19; precision=day.
Publication notes: Full paper in the KDMiLe 2026 proceedings published by SBC on its SOL open library. The PDF title page and Crossref list the same two authors in the same order. The PDF grants permission to copy without fee for non-commercial use with notice; no standard license is declared.
Publication source: https://sol.sbc.org.br/index.php/kdmile/article/view/44978

The annotation was reviewed against the publisher PDF and the Crossref deposit for its DOI. The method, In-Context Learning Guidance (ICLG), has GPT-5.1 solve tasks offline and appends its reasoning fields alone to the student prompt; the teacher's low-level actions stay outside that prompt, and teacher calls precede the student run. Evaluation serves the 130 MiniWoB++ tasks locally, caps each run at 5 minutes and 25 interaction steps, counts a score of at least 0.5 as solved, and reports single runs: seven of ten students improve and three lose one task. Retry and refined-prompt ablations cover three students. The paper names no code release or arXiv version.

The card reports 11 to 14 of 54 multi-step tasks on held-out real sites for version v19s and 22 to 27 ms per decision on one RTX 4070 Ti SUPER; these are publisher measurements. CloudCruise
Resource type: product
Review status: curated
Scope: core

Managed browser-automation platform for healthcare portals and EHRs in which a builder agent turns a chat description into a reusable workflow graph that runs in cloud VMs and a maintenance agent repairs.
Platforms: web
Topics: web-navigation, automation, workflow, robustness

Recorded specifications: {"access": "publisher-managed", "pricing_url": "https://cloudcruise.com/pricing"}

The homepage targets payer-portal and EHR workflows and says every run executes in a VM with laptop-like fingerprints and human-like input, with queued concurrency, video replay, per-action screenshots and logs, and HIPAA-compliant infrastructure. The documentation says the builder agent opens a live browser preview, navigates the target site, asks clarifying questions and turns confirmed actions into a node-and-edge graph that later runs deterministically, with model calls confined to building the graph. Click nodes target elements either by XPath or through an LLM vision mode labelled AI (Screenshot). The maintenance agent classifies failures from the error screenshot, page state and selector signals, then recovers in place, asks for input, retries or hands the workflow to the builder agent. Citrix virtual desktops are automated through their HTML5 browser client using the screenshot mode. Runs start through an API with TypeScript and Python SDKs.

Primary source: https://www.cloudcruise.com

Topics: mobile-navigation, automation, planning, self-reflection

The page (version V0.0.1) documents a DashScope endpoint for the gui-owl app that takes a screenshot URL, a task instruction, a session ID and optional operation hints (add_info), and returns the next action, such as a click or swipe with screen coordinates, with a thought and an explanation. Requests set device_type to mobile or pc and use the model pre-gui_owl_7b; the PC pipeline also names worker, manager, reflector and notetaker models and can enable the reflection and memory agents. The page states that the agent targets phones, in-car systems, TVs and PCs, names no mobile operating system, and lists usage as free for a limited time. The X-PLUG/MobileAgent README links this page as a limited-time free Mobile-Agent-v3 API; the page itself names no paper or released checkpoint, so no relation to the Mobile-Agent or GUI-Owl records is asserted. The receipt uses the Markdown export because the HTML embeds a per-request tracking ID.

text:
Grounding Multimodal Large Language Model in GUI World
Resource type: paper
Review status: curated
Scope: core

Trains a 0.4B SAM-initialized GUI grounding model on 0.5M auto-collected web screenshots with 35M element annotations, then links it to a Qwen-VL planner through a position token for MiniWob, AITW and Mind2Web.
Platforms: cross-platform, web, android
Topics: grounding, data-generation, web-navigation, mobile-navigation
Published: 2025-05-01
Authors: Weixian Lei, Difei Gao, Mike Zheng Shou

Publication edition: Grounding Multimodal Large Language Model in GUI World
Publication authors: Weixian Lei, Difei Gao, Mike Zheng Shou
Publication edition date (recorded precision): 2025-05-01
Publication venue: International Conference on Learning Representations 2025 (ICLR 2025)
Publication volume: 2025
Publication pages: 19742-19765
Publication date basis: Publisher citation_publication_date metadata on the ICLR proceedings page states 2025-05-01; precision=day.
Publication notes: The proceedings page metadata lists the authors surname first; the PDF byline order and spelling are retained. The record URL is the OpenReview forum; the proceedings page and PDF are the retained receipts. No DOI is given.
Publication source: https://openreview.net/forum?id=M9iky9Ruhx

Reviewed against the ICLR 2025 proceedings page and PDF; the OpenReview forum lists it as an ICLR 2025 Poster. The grounding model, AssistGUIGrounder (AGG), pairs a SAM-pretrained ViT image encoder and a transformer query encoder with a two-layer box decoder. The data engine loads Common Crawl pages from 118 domains in a browser such as Chrome, scrolls them with Page Down and reads element data through UI Automation; grounding training used 0.36M web images with 22M annotations after smoothing, plus 27K mobile screenshots from WidgetCaption and RICO. ScreenSpot grounding covers mobile, desktop and web screenshots; agent fine-tuning covers MiniWob, AITW and Mind2Web. The paper gives github.com/showlab/AssistGUIGround for code and data; that repository returned HTTP 404 on 2026-10-19. No arXiv version was found.

Primary source: https://openreview.net/forum?id=M9iky9Ruhx

A teacher model (for example Gemini 2.5 Pro) writes malicious reasoning trajectories drawn from a five-category malicious action library, and the agent learns them by supervised fine-tuning, which the paper calls Context-Aware Behavioral Imitation. Main results fine-tune Qwen2-VL-2B and Qwen2-VL-7B at a 0.1 poisoning ratio with a blended visual trigger; an AndroidWorld emulator deployment through Mobile-Agent-v3 is described in the supplementary material. The paper links no code release or arXiv version.

Yutori
Resource type: product
Review status: curated
Scope: core

Yutori's web-agent platform: the Navigator computer-use model API (n1.5 for browsers, n2 for full desktops), task APIs for browsing, research and Scout web monitoring, and the Delegate personal agent.
Platforms: web, desktop, macos
Topics: web-navigation, automation, tool-integration

Recorded specifications: {"access": "publisher-managed"}

Yutori was founded by Abhishek Das, Devi Parikh and Dhruv Batra and announced its seed round in March 2025. Navigator models are called through an OpenAI Chat Completions-compatible endpoint: the caller sends a screenshot and a task, the model returns actions as tool calls, and the caller executes them and sends a fresh screenshot in an agent loop. n1.5 drives browsers in a normalized 1000x1000 coordinate space with a core set of 18 coordinate-based tools or an expanded set that adds element extraction, find, set_element_value and JavaScript execution, and can return JSON matching a caller schema. n2 operates a full desktop through batched GUI actions plus bash and file tools; the SDK ships local Docker and Daytona examples, and Yutori MCP runs it on the visible macOS desktop, sending screen contents to Yutori. A Python SDK wraps the APIs, a CLI runs research, browsing and Scout tasks, and an MCP server with workflow skills exposes these tasks and computer use to coding agents. Scouts monitor the web on a schedule, and Delegate is a consumer agent meant to complete handed-off tasks independently. Yutori also publishes a computer-use leaderboards page compiling reported results for six benchmarks. The publisher describes its Online-Mind2Web figure as independently verified and its Navi-Bench v2 and Westworld figures as its own evaluations.
